_doc: my-konsole IS the systray daemon for its OWN trays. The watchdog tray is NOT here any more: my-watchdog is a separate product and ships its own StatusNotifierItem, so a machine that runs only the sampler still gets a tray and a machine running both does not get two. Each entry here becomes a real StatusNotifierItem tray icon, created natively by src-tauri/src/main.rs's setup_systrays() (Tauri's tray-icon feature) when my-konsole runs with --tray-daemon. `menu` items shell-exec `command` on click. `profile` names the my-konsole profile this tray's content mirrors (for the future --initial-profile jump-to-tab support — see _TODO). build.sh install copies this file to ~/.local/share/my-konsole/systrays.json and installs+starts a systemd --user service running `my-konsole --tray-daemon` (Restart=always) — no nix module, no separate python/GTK process. Icons are the SVGs in configs/systray-icons/ — `icon` is that basename; they are rasterised at load, so every tray has its OWN icon (they all shared the app icon before).
_TODO: my-konsole has no CLI/env initial-profile support yet — `profile` here is documentation only until that lands.

menu.label: Nix Daemon: RESET (restart)
menu.command: bash -lc 'sudo systemctl restart nix-daemon.service && notify-send "NixOS" "nix-daemon reset"'

menu.label: RESET daemon
menu.command: bash -lc 'sudo systemctl restart docker.service && notify-send "Docker" "docker daemon reset"'

trays.title: Cloud — Mesh VPN / VMs
trays.default_command: konsole --hold -e bash -lc 'sudo wg-tunnel status; echo; sudo wg show; read'

submenu.label: Tunnel: status (split/full per iface)
submenu.command: konsole --hold -e bash -lc 'sudo wg-tunnel status; read'

submenu.label: Tunnel: status JSON
submenu.command: konsole --hold -e bash -lc 'sudo wg-tunnel json | jq .; read'

submenu.label: Tunnel: TOGGLE wg0  (split <-> full)
submenu.command: sudo wg-tunnel toggle wg0 && notify-send "wg0 tunnel" "$(sudo wg-tunnel status | head -1)"

submenu.label: Tunnel: TOGGLE wg-public  (split <-> full)
submenu.command: sudo wg-tunnel toggle wg-public && notify-send "wg-public tunnel" "$(sudo wg-tunnel status | tail -1)"

submenu.label: Tunnel: wg0 -> FULL (all traffic via hub; IPv4 only)
submenu.command: sudo wg-tunnel full wg0 && notify-send "wg0" "full tunnel"

submenu.label: Tunnel: wg0 -> SPLIT (mesh only)
submenu.command: sudo wg-tunnel split wg0 && notify-send "wg0" "split tunnel"

submenu.label: Tunnel: wg-public -> FULL
submenu.command: sudo wg-tunnel full wg-public && notify-send "wg-public" "full tunnel"

submenu.label: Tunnel: wg-public -> SPLIT
submenu.command: sudo wg-tunnel split wg-public && notify-send "wg-public" "split tunnel"

submenu.label: Mesh: peers (wg show)
submenu.command: konsole --hold -e bash -lc 'sudo wg show; read'

submenu.label: Mesh: handshakes + transfer
submenu.command: konsole --hold -e bash -lc 'for i in wg0 wg-public; do echo "== $i"; sudo wg show $i latest-handshakes; sudo wg show $i transfer; done; read'

submenu.label: Mesh: addresses (v4 + v6)
submenu.command: konsole --hold -e bash -lc 'ip -brief addr show wg0; ip -brief addr show wg-public; read'

submenu.label: Mesh: routes (v4)
submenu.command: konsole --hold -e bash -lc 'ip route show table all | grep -E "wg0|wg-public|^default"; read'

submenu.label: Mesh: routes (v6)
submenu.command: konsole --hold -e bash -lc 'ip -6 route show table all | grep -E "wg0|wg-public|^default"; read'

submenu.label: Mesh: endpoints (hub IP:port)
submenu.command: konsole --hold -e bash -lc 'sudo wg show wg0 endpoints; sudo wg show wg-public endpoints; read'

submenu.label: Check: ping hubs (IPv4)
submenu.command: konsole --hold -e bash -lc 'ping -c3 10.0.0.1; echo; ping -c3 10.1.0.1; read'

submenu.label: Check: ping hubs (IPv6 ULA)
submenu.command: konsole --hold -e bash -lc 'ping -c3 fd0c:1d00::1; echo; ping -c3 fd0c:1d01::1; read'

submenu.label: Check: public egress IP (who am I)
submenu.command: konsole --hold -e bash -lc 'echo "v4: $(curl -s -4 -m 8 ifconfig.co || echo none)"; echo "v6: $(curl -s -6 -m 8 ifconfig.co || echo none)"; read'

submenu.label: Check: mesh DNS A + AAAA
submenu.command: konsole --hold -e bash -lc 'for n in diegonmarcos.com auth.diegonmarcos.com maddy.app; do echo "== $n"; dig +short $n A; dig +short $n AAAA; done; read'

submenu.label: Check: which stack does a name use?
submenu.command: konsole --hold -e bash -lc 'getent ahosts diegonmarcos.com; echo; echo "(::ffff:x = IPv4-mapped, fd0c: = mesh IPv6)"; read'

submenu.label: NM: active connections
submenu.command: konsole --hold -e bash -lc 'nmcli -f NAME,DEVICE,TYPE,STATE connection show --active; read'

submenu.label: NM: wireguard profiles
submenu.command: konsole --hold -e bash -lc 'nmcli -f NAME,UUID,TYPE,AUTOCONNECT connection show | grep -iE "wireguard|wg"; read'

submenu.label: NM: restart wg0
submenu.command: sudo nmcli connection down wg0; sudo nmcli connection up wg0

submenu.label: NM: restart wg-public
submenu.command: sudo nmcli connection down wg-public; sudo nmcli connection up wg-public

submenu.label: WG: endpoint primary/fallback
submenu.command: konsole --hold -e bash -lc 'wg-fallback status; read'

trays.title: my-webserver — local file server
trays._doc: my-webserver is deployed by home-manager (ba_flakes_desktop/src/modules/my-webserver/default.nix) as BOTH a PID-file wrapper (~/.local/bin/my-webserver) and a systemd --user unit, which both want :8000. This menu drives the wrapper, because that is the one actually running today (the unit ships disabled), and shows the unit state next to it so the split is visible rather than a mystery when the two fight over the port.

menu.label: Who holds :8000
menu.command: konsole --hold -e bash -lc "ss -tulpn | grep :8000 || echo \"nothing listening on 8000\"; read"
